Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Growth and value shares are set for an overhaul after S&P Dow Jones Indices adopted new rules on how to sort equities into the two investment styles.
The index provider will add intangible assets, forward earnings and free cash flow to the list of factors to define whether a company is cheap relative to its share price, according to a statement Friday. At the same time, 12-month price momentum will be dropped as a criteria to rank a company’s growth potential.

item.title: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
item.description:
Oct 23rd, 2026
Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. He calls the matchup evidence for the players’ union that success is possible without a salary cap, while cautioning that owners may dismiss it as an unsustainable exception: smaller-market teams have little margin for error and can lose players to wealthier clubs in free agency. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close."

item.description:

How Valterra's Forging the Future of Platinum | Chief Financial Officer
Chief Financial Officers now play a critical role in shaping corporate strategy and positioning organizations to meet future challenges. This episode profiles Valterra Platinum CFO Sayurie Naidoo, who leads the world's largest company producing platinum group metals. One year after its demerger from Anglo American, the South African firm is looking ahead to develop new markets for PGMs as the adoption of battery electric vehicles threatens their primary area of demand. Data centers face potential credit rating downgrades due to moratoriums and cancellations driven by public opposition, according to S&P Global Ratings.
Delays due to grid capacity constraints, environmental sustainability concerns and zoning shifts “could increase downward pressure on the creditworthiness of data center projects,” analysts including Chris Mooney wrote in a report Friday.

item.title: San Diego to Leave Muni Bond Group After SEC Oversight Concerns
item.description: The city of San Diego said it plans to withdraw from a group that helps issue and manage billions of dollars in municipal bonds after federal regulators raised concerns about the organization’s oversight.

item.title: Chipmakers Post Longest Weekly Drop Since November
item.description: A resurgence in oil prices dragged down stocks and bonds, stoking concerns about inflation just days ahead of the Federal Reserve decision on interest rates. Brent crude settled near $117 as a flare-up in Middle East violence threatened supplies. Most S&P 500 firms fell even as selling pressure on tech shares abated. A gauge of chipmakers edged up, but posted its longest weekly drop since November. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 1.2%. Treasuries relinquished a portion of the previous session’s rally. Co-Host of Odd Lots, Joe Weisenthal says it's important to the US Economy that tech companies fire on all cylinders. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hedge Funds Are Record Short Natural Gas on Mild Winter Outlook
item.description: Hedge-fund managers have amassed a record short position in US natural gas on expectations for an unusually mild northern winter that points to anemic demand for the furnace and power-plant fuel.
